title: categories.features
description: Request the resolved feature definitions (own + inherited) for a category. The result is cacheable by the returned revision; a category.changed event invalidates it. This object validates the request payload; the response shape ({category_id, revision, features:[ResolvedFeature]}) is documented in $defs for consumers.

category_id.description: ID of the category whose feature schema to resolve.

ResolvedFeature.description: One resolved feature in the response 'features' array. Fed to stapel-attributes' coerce_feature_defs / FeatureDef. Every property of the canon (stapel-attributes docs/feature-def.schema.json $defs.FeatureDef) except 'config' — which has its own per-type shape there — MUST be present here; tests/test_resolved_feature_contract.py gates that. show_at_title, show_as_badge and translate carry the title/badge projections attributes' dto_to_dao builds; 'rules' carries requiredness and conditional show/hide, without which the whole category silently reverts to static 'mandatory'; 'visibility' carries the disclosure axis stapel-listings stamps onto every stored value at write time — a definition arriving without it stamps 'public', which publishes the VIN the axis exists to keep off a public page.

slug.description: Payload key the feature is submitted under.

mandatory.description: Whether a value is STATICALLY required; conditional requirement comes from 'rules'.

show_at_title.description: Whether the value is shown in the listing title.

show_as_badge.description: Whether the value is shown as a badge.

visibility.description: Which audience may READ a stored value. Orthogonal to 'mandatory': a non-public feature is still required, still validated, still stored and still moderated — it is only never handed to a reader who is not entitled to it. Identifiers of a specific physical unit (VIN, IMEI, a serial or a registry number) belong here. 'owner' = the object's owner, and staff; 'staff' = staff only, not even the owner's own view. A non-public feature is never in a title, never a badge, never indexed and never facetable, and show_at_title/show_as_badge are forced to false. Default: "public" (a definition that says nothing keeps behaving as it did before this axis existed).

rules.description: Conditional rules over sibling values, in stapel-attributes' closed grammar ($defs.Rule of the canon). Default: [] (no rules — requiredness is 'mandatory', the feature is always visible).

description.description: Help text under the field; translation key or literal. Default: "" (no help text).

example.description: Placeholder text; translation key or literal. Default: "" (no placeholder).

default.description: Initial form value in DTO 'value' shape (for a select, a list of option codes); any JSON. Default: null (the form starts empty).

hints.description: Notices rendered with the field; titles and contents are translation keys or literals. Default: [] (no notices).

group.description: Form section this feature belongs to; sections order by first appearance. Default: "" (the unnamed leading section).

config.description: Type-specific config (merged with type defaults), with a 'type' discriminator. Also carries the ENGINE-LEVEL keys no type's config declares and stapel-attributes' unknown-key warning allowlists (validation.ENGINE_CONFIG_KEYS): 'facet' — false when this category does NOT offer the feature as a buyer filter axis. ABSENT means true, so a definition that says nothing keeps behaving as it did before the axis existed. It is what a category author says about a field no library can classify from its type: the parcel's weight/length/height/width and the wholesale block are metadata about the SALE, while the very same 'int' one category over is a real filter.
